To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best performing curriculum learning approach for sequence prediction is to start with the most general task, followed by the most specific task, and finally the most general task again.

(1) incremental curriculum learning, where the difficulty of the learning task is increased over time, is the most successful form of curriculum learning in the context considered, (2) the most effective form of incremental learning is to increase the complexity of the task over time, and (3) the most effective way to achieve this is by gradually increasing the length of the sequences to be learned.

(a) curriculum learning is not always better than random ordering, (b) curriculum learning with a fixed ordering is always better than curriculum learning with a random ordering, (c) curriculum learning with an adaptive ordering is always better or as good as curriculum learning with a static ordering, and (d) curriculum learning with adaptive ordering is better than curriculum learning in a fixed ordering when the difficulty of the tasks increases over time
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) What is the effect of incremental or curriculum sequence learning in the context RNNs? 2) What are the best ways to implement incremental or curriculum learning for RNNs?
the following questions: (i) Can we improve learning of generative RNN models for sequence learning by using an incremental approach, where the complexity of the problem is increased over time?
the question of how to improve the learning of generative RNN models by incrementally increasing the complexity or difficulty of the problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
incremental learning is beneficial for the learning of sequence models.
the incremental learning strategy which performs the best is the one which starts with a simple task and then incrementally adds more complexity to the task in a controlled and gradual way.
the best performance is obtained by starting with a simple task, and gradually increasing the difficulty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that incremental learning is a powerful technique for sequence learning, but that the form in which the incrementality is introduced has a strong impact on the performance of the resulting model, and the best form depends on the problem at hand.

we have shown that the most effective form of incremental learning is to increase the difficulty by increasing the scope of the task, and that it is not necessarily beneficial to increase the difficulty of the task.
incremental sequence learning is a promising approach for improving sequence prediction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is not possible to draw general conclusions about the effect of incremental sequence learning, and that the choice of learning method is crucial for the success or failure of incremental sequence learning.
it is important to consider the form and timing of incremental or curriculum presentation.
it is important to carefully select the learning schedule, and to ensure that the incremental learning schedule is compatible with the model architecture.
